brief.topic: ZAgenticOPN Experience Version conformance comparison: Routa versus qm

criteria.question: What primary evidence shows that one Agent can publish available work and another Agent can discover it after a task-agnostic Human trigger, without the Human naming a Work Item or copying context?
What primary evidence shows atomic competing claim semantics in which concurrent Agents cannot both obtain execution authority or execute the same Work Item?
What primary evidence shows that an executing Agent can publish result summary, acceptance status, next action, blocker and canonical Git references for another Agent to read?
What primary evidence shows that a reviewer Agent can discover and atomically claim awaiting review, verify the referenced result and complete review without Human context supplementation?
What evidence shows the system reports no eligible work and filter reasons instead of inventing work or requiring the Human to select a Work Item?
What evidence shows missing acceptance, result or references become an observable classified defect rather than being treated as a successful handoff?
How does the project isolate default coordination queries by project or workspace while preserving explicit cross-project navigation when allowed?
How does the project separate Agent-private recovery context from shared coordination facts, and what evidence supports recovery after an Agent interruption?
Which product semantics, state models, identity boundaries, acceptance rules and lifecycle responsibilities would remain owned by ZAgenticOPN versus the candidate?
What evidence shows the candidate can support the narrow Experience Version, and what adapter, deployment, upgrade, license or maintenance costs would be introduced?
